title: /sessions/read discloses effective agent provider and whether MOE_AGENT_COMMAND overrode it
description:
SPIDR grandchild E of task-8e793ae3c63f41189bcc05f6d7c15605 (architect-2e480458, 2026-09-05). dependsOn grandchild D (effective provider is whatever spawn actually resolved).

WHAT THIS ROW OWNS: extend SessionsView so the operator can see which provider is running and that MOE_AGENT_COMMAND overrode the browser setting when it did. Daemon handler apps/daemon/src/http/sessions-read.ts (172 lines) plus decoder apps/control-room/src/live/live-sessions.ts (SESSIONS_FRAME_KEYS currently [concurrency, outcome, readAt, sessions, totals, unreadable]). Nested object preferred, mirroring SessionsConcurrency: e.g. agentProvider: { effective, envOverride } with exact keys at that level.

NOT IN SCOPE: Seats rendering (child 3), spawn argv, command kind, store writes.

VERIFY: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test` AND `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test` (decoder lives in apps/control-room; a bare pnpm test covers neither).

Concurrent: task-92d84d38 (DONE) already added concurrency to this read; live-sessions.ts:133 pins ["activeSeats", "configuredAgentLimit"]. Do not regress that.
definitionOfDone: POST /sessions/read success JSON includes the effective provider and whether an env override is in force. A test with MOE_AGENT_COMMAND set and the durable setting saying the other provider asserts both the effective provider AND the override flag. A test with the env unset asserts the override flag is false and the effective provider matches the setting.

live-sessions.ts decodes the new member(s) under exact-key rules. A test that adds an extra key or drops a key on the new nested object (if nested) returns ERROR SESSIONS_RESPONSE_INVALID at CONTROL_ROOM_LIVE_SESSIONS. SESSIONS_FRAME_KEYS and the daemon SessionsView members stay in lockstep — the existing live-sessions.test.ts source-text pin against sessions-read.ts must stay green.
Gates quoted with `Test Files N passed`: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test`, `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test`, `pnpm typecheck`. Root `pnpm test` is NOT evidence for either apps/** package.
taskRails: EXACT-KEY: live-sessions.ts SESSIONS_FRAME_KEYS is exact-arity. Adding a member on the daemon and not the decoder BLANKS the Seats screen. Move sessions-read.ts and live-sessions.ts in the SAME commit.
THE ENV OVERRIDE IS DISCLOSED, NEVER SILENT. Assert the disclosure fields, not just that argv followed the env.
Do not edit Seats UI (child 3 task-c090faae owns the screen). Do not rebuild spawn resolution (grandchild D).

comments.content:
THE FILE THIS ROW EDITS ALREADY DOCUMENTS ITS CENTRAL PROBLEM. architect-b63fabf3, 2026-09-05, HEAD f3b94eaa. Plan approved: 5 steps, 4 files, no new files, no split.

The row's proposed shape (`agentProvider: { effective, envOverride }`, nested, mirroring `SessionsConcurrency`) measured correct and the plan keeps it. What the description leaves open is the **naming**, and that is the substance here.

## The daemon cannot observe what the wrapper resolved

`sessions-read.ts:29-35`, three lines above where this member goes, on `configuredAgentLimit`:

> "CONFIGURED, never observed… The daemon and the wrapper are **separate processes**; `moe up` spawns both from one child environment, so in the launched configuration they agree. A daemon started standalone, or beside a wrapper launched separately with a different value, reports a limit no wrapper is honouring. **Nothing here measures the wrapper.**"

`MOE_AGENT_COMMAND` read inside the daemon is the **daemon's** env. A member called bare `effective` reads to an operator as "what is actually running" — which this endpoint cannot know. The plan requires the name and docblock to carry that limit exactly as `configuredAgentLimit` does. That is the file's own precedent, not an invention.

Note the split in what *is* knowable: the durable project setting is genuinely read from the store and is authoritative; the env override is only the daemon's own environment. The docblock has to say which half is which.

## A second limit, stated rather than papered

`createSessionsReadPort` destructures `{ projectId, store }` and never takes a goal — the read is **project-scoped**. So this member can disclose the project default plus the env override, but **not** a per-goal override, which grandchild C's store does support. The plan forbids adding a goal parameter to a project-scoped read to reach it, and requires the limit be stated in the completion record.

## The member name is constrained by a regex in another package's test

`live-sessions.test.ts:63-75` reads `sessions-read.ts` **as source text** (the control room must never import apps/daemon), then collects members with:

```
/^ {2}readonly (?<name>[A-Za-z]+)[?]?:/gmu
```

Letters only, anchored at two-space indent. A name with a digit or underscore, or a member nested a level deeper, is **invisible to the pin** — which then passes while the two rosters silently disagree. Not a red; a hole. `agentProvider` is fine.

## The failure mode is a blank screen, not a red test

`SESSIONS_FRAME_KEYS` is exact-arity (`exactDataRecord` at :129). A daemon member without its decoder key makes the whole frame decode as `SESSIONS_RESPONSE_INVALID` — the constant's own docblock says it "does not degrade the Seats screen, it **BLANKS** it". That is why this is a same-commit rule, and drill (i) proves both directions of it.

## Two smaller things the plan pins

- **A truthiness check on the override flag** would admit any non-empty string and pass every happy-path arm. The file's own `typeof record.unreadable !== "boolean"` at :130 is the model; drill (iii) proves the guard is real.
- **`pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test` is mandatory.** Two of the four files live in apps/control-room, and no other gate sees them — not root `pnpm test` (no `apps/**` in the include), not `pnpm typecheck` (runtime value checks), not the daemon leg. Same trap that blocked task-40e52fa8 once. It is the named `complete_task` command for that reason.

One thing left to the worker deliberately: the env may hold a **path** (`/usr/local/bin/codex`) rather than a bare name — the pause gate already normalises with `providerFor(...)?.leaf`. Whether the disclosure reports the leaf or the raw value is a real operator-facing choice, and step 5 requires it be made and stated.

The plan keeps it. What the description does NOT settle, and what this plan decides, is the NAMING and the two claim-limits behind it.

CHOSEN - NAME THE MEMBERS SO THEY CANNOT OVERSTATE THE CLAIM. sessions-read.ts:29-35 already documents the identical problem for `configuredAgentLimit`, verbatim: "CONFIGURED, never observed... The daemon and the wrapper are SEPARATE PROCESSES... NOTHING HERE MEASURES THE WRAPPER." `MOE_AGENT_COMMAND` read inside the daemon is the DAEMON's env; it agrees with the wrapper only in the `moe up` launched configuration. A member called bare `effective` reads to an operator as "what is actually running", which this endpoint cannot know. The plan requires the name and docblock to carry that limit the way `configuredAgentLimit` does - the file's own precedent, not an invention.
REJECTED - flattening the two facts into top-level members: the lockstep pin at live-sessions.test.ts:72 matches TOP-LEVEL members at two-space indent, so two flat members means two frame keys and two decoder guards, for facts that belong together. Nested is one key, one guard, and mirrors concurrency.
REJECTED - having the daemon ASK the wrapper what it resolved: there is no such channel, and inventing one is far outside a disclosure row. The honest answer is to name the fact as configured-and-derived.
REJECTED - adding a goal parameter to /sessions/read so the per-goal override could be disclosed: the read is project-scoped by construction (`createSessionsReadPort` takes projectId, no goal). The limit is stated instead.
REJECTED - re-implementing precedence here: grandchild D owns `resolveAgentProvider`. This row discloses the same rule, and a second copy is how the disclosure and the spawn drift apart.
REJECTED - touching the Seats screen: task-c090faae owns rendering, and this row's rail forbids it. The decoder is the boundary.
NO SPLIT: four files, two of them tests, nothing near the line cap. The daemon member and the decoder MUST land in one commit - see risks.
